meta.title: SkiPick — Compare Japan Ski Resorts
meta.description: Browse Tokyo-area ski resorts on a map and compare prices, runs, and travel time side by side.

footer.note: SkiPick · Data maintained by the community and official sources

home.subtitle:
Stop cross-checking five different sites. 
Resort areas are outlined right on the map — pick one and compare price, runs, and travel time at a glance.
home.feature1Desc: Resort boundaries are overlaid on a real terrain map, so location, size, and nearby resorts are obvious at a glance — not just a lone pin.
home.feature2Desc: Pick 2–4 resorts and see price, run mix, lift count, and travel time laid out together — like comparing flights.
home.feature3Desc: Gondola status, today's snow conditions — the details official sites never update, added by whoever's actually on the mountain.
home.newsIntro: Website updates, release notes, and feature changes.

news.pageSubtitle: Latest updates, website changes, and release notes.

2026-08-06.title: Version 0.5 is Updated
2026-08-06.excerpt: SkiPick 0.5 is now live! Currently in testing, it only supports ski resorts near Tokyo.
2026-08-06.content:
This is a one-person project, so please be patient with the limited time available.
The current version only supports ski resorts near Tokyo. Data is based on official information for the 25-26 season, and 26-27 season data has not yet been updated.

Future development plans:
- Early-bird data for the 26-27 season
- Support for community feedback features
- Support for ski resorts nationwide

site-refresh-2026-08.title: Website refresh and new home experience
site-refresh-2026-08.excerpt: The homepage has been redesigned with a more visual resort overview and clearer comparison entry points.
site-refresh-2026-08.content: We refreshed the overall visual style of the site, strengthened the map-driven entry experience, and improved the hero section so new visitors can understand the product faster. The featured resort preview and the latest updates are now displayed more clearly on the homepage.

compare-flow-update.title: Comparison flow improved for quicker decisions
compare-flow-update.excerpt: The compare experience now highlights the most useful metrics first, making side-by-side decisions faster.
compare-flow-update.content: We reorganized the compare screen so travel time, price, and run mix are easier to scan. This makes it simpler to shortlist resorts before you decide which one to visit.

map-guidance-update.title: Map guidance and resort detail improvements
map-guidance-update.excerpt: A clearer overview and better guidance were added to the resort map and detail pages.
map-guidance-update.content: We refined the map interaction flow and added more direct guidance on how to explore resort details. The result is a smoother experience for users who want to discover specific ski areas quickly.

map.title: Resort Map
map.subtitle: Click a shaded area on the map to see resort details.

echigo-yuzawa.title: Echigo-Yuzawa
echigo-yuzawa.summary: Directly connected to Tokyo via Shinkansen. A premier ski hub packed with top destinations like GALA Yuzawa and Naeba, with fantastic hot springs.

numata-katashina.title: Numata / Katashina
numata-katashina.summary: Located in northern Gunma Prefecture, highly accessible by car. Renowned for natural powder snow and terrain variety like Kawaba and Oze Iwakura.

karuizawa.title: Karuizawa
karuizawa.summary: Just 1 hour from Tokyo by Shinkansen with early-season artificial snow setup. Features a massive luxury outlet mall and resort hotels, perfect for beginners and vacationers.

compare.title: Compare
compare.subtitle: Select up to {max} resorts to compare side by side. Departure point is fixed to Tokyo Station.
compare.emptyHint: Select at least one resort to start comparing.
compare.emptyMetrics: Select at least one data point to display.

gala-yuzawa.name: GALA Yuzawa
gala-yuzawa.summary: Connected directly to the shinkansen station, so there's almost no transfer time — the classic Tokyo day-trip pick.

naeba.name: Naeba
naeba.summary: A large resort linked by gondola to the Kagura area, good for skiers who want a mix of terrain.

kagura.name: Kagura
kagura.summary: Known for its powder and natural terrain, with the Tashiro, Kagura, and Mitsumata areas connected. Long season.

kawaba.name: Kawaba
kawaba.summary: No direct shinkansen, but an easy exit off the Kan-etsu Expressway — a favorite among drivers.

oze-iwakura.name: Oze Iwakura
oze-iwakura.summary: A 120-person gondola and excellent summit views make this a popular pick with families.

karuizawa-prince.name: Karuizawa Prince
karuizawa-prince.summary: Gentle slopes with a small vertical drop, paired with the outlet mall next door — a top choice for beginners and families.

kandatsu.name: Kandatsu Snow Resort
kandatsu.summary: Famous for all-night skiing and terrain parks, close to Yuzawa station and popular with younger skiers and snowboarders.

iwappara.name: Iwappara
iwappara.summary: Features a famous ultra-wide single-slope run with gentle gradient, ideal for beginners and family practice.

yuzawa-park.name: Yuzawa Park
yuzawa-park.summary: A hotel-ski slopes direct resort. Compact and sheltered from wind, great for kids and relaxed practice.

yuzawa-nakazato.name: Yuzawa Nakazato
yuzawa-nakazato.summary: Directly connected to JR Echigo-Nakazato Station, featuring train carriage rest areas and a fun kids park.

yuzawa-kogen.name: Yuzawa Kogen
yuzawa-kogen.summary: Access the summit via one of the world's largest 166-person ropeways. Summit links to GALA while base offers gentle slopes.

naspa-ski-garden.name: NASPA Ski Garden
naspa-ski-garden.summary: A rare skiers-only resort (no snowboards allowed) with immaculately groomed runs for peaceful skiing.

ishiuchi-maruyama.name: Ishiuchi Maruyama
ishiuchi-maruyama.summary: A classic historic resort equipped with modern hybrid lifts (Sunrise Express) and outstanding night skiing.

maiko.name: Maiko Snow Resort
maiko.summary: Just 1 minute off the Shiozawa-Ishiuchi IC. Spans 3 areas with a maximum run length of 6,000 meters.

joetsu-kokusai.name: Joetsu Kokusai
joetsu-kokusai.summary: A massive mega-resort with 4 main zones and the iconic Green Plaza Hotel right at the foot of the slopes.

hakkaisan.name: Muikamachi Hakkaisan
hakkaisan.summary: 800m vertical drop, steep inclines, and deep un-groomed powder fields make this a haven for experts.

itsukamachi.name: Itsukamachi
itsukamachi.summary: A local, cozy resort with gentle slopes, uncrowded trails, and affordable prices.

muika.name: Muika Snow Resort
muika.summary: Offers a main slope over 200m wide alongside un-groomed powder zones, overlooking the Hakkaisan peaks.
